INVESTIGATIVE AVENUES

Common tracing methods

These are investigative avenues, not promises of recovery. iForce Hackers will only use methods that are lawful and appropriately authorized.

Digital & transaction records

For financial and digital assets, analysis may identify transaction paths or service endpoints where records are available.

Identifiers & ownership records

Serial numbers, IMEI numbers, VINs, tracking numbers, registration details, and ownership documentation can provide investigative leads.

Tracking & telematics

Approved GPS, Bluetooth, device-management, telematics, and other tracking services may assist where available and lawfully accessible.

Provider & authority cooperation

Some records require cooperation from carriers, exchanges, platforms, businesses, or relevant authorities, and legal process may be required.

CASE PREPARATION

What iForce Hackers may need

  • Proof of ownership or a lawful connection to the asset.
  • Serial number, VIN, IMEI, wallet address, transaction hash, tracking number, or other available identifier.
  • Relevant dates, locations, account details, and supporting records.
  • Authorization to conduct the investigation and contact appropriate providers or authorities where required.

What “possibly recover” means

Tracing can produce a lead, identify a transaction path, locate a registered record, or establish evidence that assists a lawful recovery process. Some assets cannot be located or recovered, records may be unavailable, and third-party cooperation or legal process may be required.

No recovery result is guaranteed. iForce Hackers should communicate findings, limitations, and next steps based on the evidence available.
